rootCauses.summary: The lineage read-side resolves PREY metadata but renders only glyph and power name, discarding the canonical effect description.
rootCauses.observationEvidence: 05-lineage shows 「雫 命の余熱」 with no effect explanation.
rootCauses.sourceEvidence: PREY.traveller.desc is 「捕食時の回復が増える。喰らった息が次の狩りを支える。」 while chips() renders only data.glyph and data.power.
rootCauses.prediction: Rendering the canonical desc beside each acquired power makes the earned ability understandable without introducing new mechanics.
rootCauses.falsifier: After still omits the effect, shows effects for unowned powers, or invents text not present in PREY.

rootCauses.summary: The current compact chip representation has no semantic/visual slot for a power effect, so adding raw text inline would blur power identity and effect.
rootCauses.observationEvidence: 05-lineage presents the acquired power as a single compact chip among life metrics and adaptation rows.
rootCauses.sourceEvidence: chips() emits one flat span per item and has no effect element/class.
rootCauses.prediction: A small structured power row keeps glyph/name prominent and canonical effect secondary while preserving the rest of the lineage sheet.
rootCauses.falsifier: The effect wraps into unrelated sections or displaces current-life stake/metrics at the tested viewport.

hypothesis.cause: Canonical power meaning already exists but the lineage projection discards it and its flat chip layout cannot communicate effect hierarchy.
hypothesis.prediction: Projecting PREY.desc into a structured acquired-power row will let players understand what the earned memory does while leaving progression authority untouched.
hypothesis.falsifier: Same-condition After does not make the effect legible, displays unowned powers, or obscures current-life progress/stakes.

candidates.reason: Uses existing PREY authority at the existing memory surface; no new rule or persistent state.
Adds combat clutter and conflates permanent memory with active hunt growth/stakes, which already have dedicated feedback.

implementation.summary: Render only acquired powers as structured lineage entries using canonical PREY glyph/name/desc, with scoped styling and no progression/runtime mutation.

workItems.summary: Keep power meaning sourced directly from PREY and render it only for acquired current/past-life power keys.
workItems.evidence: Leaf rendering tests cover acquired, unowned and unknown keys and assert canonical desc text.
workItems.expectedPlayerFacingEffect: An earned power has a readable meaning instead of a name-only badge.

workItems.summary: Give acquired powers a dedicated name/effect hierarchy scoped to lineage without changing other chips or sheet structure.
workItems.evidence: Scoped markup/style assertions plus immutable same-condition lineage screenshot.
workItems.expectedPlayerFacingEffect: The power name remains scannable and the effect is readable without crowding life metrics or active-hunt stake text.

limitations: Leaf tests cannot establish visual readability; immutable native-play screenshot is required.
Hosted SwiftShader is not a physical-device benchmark.

workItemCoverage.evidence: Leaf render assertions plus actual acquired traveller power in immutable After.
